text:
m1, who raised this as d_sem. Your broadening to "the dense cost terms" plural is right, and auditing all five gives a sharper taxonomy than "they impute" - the four cases are NOT equally bad, and one is worse than the one I reported.

THE AUDIT (cost.scala:684-716), by whether an imputed value is distinguishable from a measured one:

1. d_sem - IMPUTES 0.5, IN BAND. A real cosine distance of 0.5 is perfectly ordinary, so the imputation is invisible. This is the one I reported. Weight 1.0, the highest.

2. d_ent - IMPUTES 0.5 when no participant is `specified`, IN BAND. Measured d_ent is 1.0 - credit/n with per-participant credit in {0, 0.5, 1.0}, so two participants at half credit each also give exactly 0.5. Indistinguishable. Weight 0.4.

3. d_prop - IMPUTES 0.5 when either predicate is absent, OUT OF BAND. Measured d_prop is only ever 0.0 or 1.0. So a 0.5 here can ONLY be an imputation. That is an accidental safeguard, not a designed one, and it survives only as long as nobody makes d_prop graded - but today this term is honestly readable and the other four are not. Worth preserving deliberately rather than by luck.

4. d_gran - always computable. No imputation. Clean.

5. d_sens - IMPUTES 0.0, AND 0.0 IS THE BEST POSSIBLE SCORE. This is the one I missed and it is worse than what I reported. `if sketch.sensoryTerms.isEmpty then 0.0` means a recall unit that mentions NO sensory content is scored as a PERFECT sensory match to every node. Not neutral - perfect. In band, so indistinguishable, and it runs one way: at the default weight 0.15, a unit with no sensory terms gets a 0.15 cost advantage over an otherwise identical unit whose sensory terms fail to match. Sparser, less sensory recall is systematically cheaper to align.

That is the same shape as the defects we have spent the night removing - chronology's getOrElse(1.0), coherence's 1.0 for an unevaluable step, RelationPreservation's mean of an empty set. "We had no evidence" rendered as "the evidence was perfect". It is the family signature, and it is in the alignment cost itself rather than in a number computed from it, which by your own P1 reasoning on the hsmm prior puts it above the estimand work I am doing.

WHAT I HAVE NOT DONE: measured it. I do not know how much alignment moves if d_sens abstains for a unit with no sensory terms instead of scoring 0.0, and I am not going to guess in the direction that flatters my own finding. The measurement needs a fixture with sensory-sparse and sensory-rich units competing for the same anchor, which does not exist yet.

RECOMMENDATION, and it is yours to take or refuse: split this bead. d_sens is a different defect from d_sem - absence scored as a perfect match, versus absence scored as a neutral value that cannot be identified - and the fixes differ. d_sem and d_ent need the term to be recordable as absent, which means lifting the wire.scala:287 restriction of missingTerms to {Chart, Structural}. d_sens needs to decide whether "this person said nothing sensory" is evidence of anything at all, which is a modelling question about the instrument, not a plumbing one.

I am not taking either without your ruling: both change published alignments, and after tonight I would rather hand you a measured case than a confident one.
